newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain wants Ebro sold to savings banks - press.
newsitem.headline: Spain wants Ebro sold to savings banks - press.

text.p: The Spanish government is pressurising the Kuwait Investment Office (KIO) to sell its 39 percent stake in sugar firm Ebro Agricolas to national savings banks, newspaper reports said on Monday.
KIO also owns 21 percent of sugar firm Azucarera with which Ebro started talks on a possible merger last year.
The government appears to be interested in maintaining the merged company's Spanish character.
Possible buyers for the Ebro stake, worth up to around 45 billion pesetas ($306 million), were regional savings bank Caja de Madrid, and the Cajas of Castille and Leon, the reports said.
Last week, stock market watchdog CNMV said the governing Popular Party (PP) had issued a parliamentary proposal setting out reasons the PP considered valid for the merger to be postponed.
The PP statement said it would like the final structure of the new group to "guarantee the company's future (within) Agro-industrial activity and its Spanish nature".
This was after France's Saint-Louis's Generale Sucriere, a stakeholder in both Spanish companies, expressed interest in controlling the new group.
